title: The Road to Decarbonising Our Corporations
what_it_is: The Road to Decarbonising Our Corporations

sections.label: Revised carbon emissions targets
sections.summary: The Government announced revised targets peaking at 65 MtCO2e, tapering to 60 MtCO2e by the decade's end, for net-zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Following these debates, the Government announced revised targets for our long-term carbon footprint, peaking at 65 megatons of carbon dioxide emissions (MtCO2e) over the next few years, before tapering down to 60 MtCO2e by the end of the decade, to achieve the net-zero target by 2050.

sections.label: Carbon tax rate increases
sections.summary: The carbon tax was raised to $25 per megaton, will step up to $45 in 2026, and reach $50 to $80 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The bluntest measure for addressing emissions is our carbon tax.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This was recently raised to $25 per megaton, from a miserable $5 and, will step up to $45 in 2026, before reaching a range of between $50 and $80 by 2030.

sections.label: Fifty facilities emit most carbon
sections.summary: An estimated four-fifths of Singapore's carbon emissions come from just 50 facilities in manufacturing, power, water and waste.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the overwhelming majority, an estimated four-fifths of carbon emissions, are accounted for by just 50 facilities, spread across the manufacturing, power, water and waste.

sections.label: Mandatory climate-related disclosures
sections.summary: Listed companies must make mandatory climate-related disclosures consistent with the ISSB by 2025, extending to large non-listed companies by 2027.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, listed companies will be required to make mandatory climate-related disclosures, consistent with the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), by 2025; and this will extend to large non-listed companies by 2027.

sections.label: GreenGov.SG reporting effort
sections.summary: The Government commenced its reporting effort in 2023 with the GreenGov.SG report.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Government commenced its reporting effort in 2023, with the GreenGov.SG report.

sections.label: Sustainability courses under SkillsFuture
sections.summary: Sustainability-related courses supported by SkillsFuture Singapore almost doubled to nearly 500 in 2023, up from about 250 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The number of sustainability-related courses supported by SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) almost doubled to nearly 500 in 2023, up from about 250 in 2022.

sections.label: Green jobs estimate
sections.summary: A study by Arup and Oxford Economics estimates up to 170,000 green-related jobs across all sectors by next year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A study by Arup and Oxford Economics estimates that there could be as many as 170,000 green-related jobs, across all sectors, by next year.

sections.label: Sustainability professionals conversion programme
sections.summary: Workforce Singapore launched a Career Conversion Programme for Sustainability Professionals in December 2022 to support SMEs pursuing sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Workforce Singapore launched a Career Conversion Programme for Sustainability Professionals (CCP-S) in December 2022, aimed at supporting SMEs in their pursuit of sustainability.

sections.label: Green loans and bonds growth
sections.summary: Green, social and sustainability loans and bonds have grown, and government green bond issuance is expected to reach $35 billion by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Green, social and sustainability loans have exploded to $30.4 billion last year from just $3.3 billion six years ago; as has bonds, rising from $1 billion to $7.4 billion over the same period.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: By 2030, the Government and statutory boards are expected to issue green bonds that amount to $35 billion, up from $2.1 billion last year.

sections.label: Broadening carbon tax and reporting
sections.summary: The passage calls for broadening the carbon tax base and transparent reporting supplemented by workers with green skills.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, we need to broaden the base for carbon taxation, both to include smaller players as well as stages higher and lower in a firm's value chain.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, we have to monitor our progress with transparent reporting, which, in turn, has to be supplemented by workers with green skills.

sections.label: Singapore net zero direction
sections.summary: Singapore states it will do its part in international climate efforts and has set a direction to reach net zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Amidst international efforts to address climate change, Singapore must and in fact, we will do our part.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We have set a clear direction to reach net zero by 2050.

sections.label: Carbon tax large emitters
sections.summary: The carbon tax currently targets large direct emitters responsible for about 80% of total carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Today, the carbon tax targets large direct emitters responsible for about 80% of our total carbon emissions.

sections.label: Carbon price by 2030
sections.summary: The carbon price is scheduled to reach $50 to $80 per tonne of CO2-equivalent by 2030, aligned with Singapore's international climate commitment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The carbon price is scheduled to reach $50 to $80 per tonne of CO2-equivalent by 2030 which is aligned with our international climate commitment and sets a clear direction in our decarbonisation journey.

sections.label: Low carbon electricity imports
sections.summary: Singapore has raised its ambition to import up to six gigawatts of low carbon electricity by 2035, up from four gigawatts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Second, as the Member knows, we have raised our ambition to import up to six gigawatts of low carbon electricity by 2035 up from the current four gigawatts.

sections.label: Enterprise Development Grant Sustainability
sections.summary: The Enterprise Development Grant – Sustainability provides up to 70% support for sustainability projects, higher than other project categories.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: They can also use the Enterprise Development Grant – Sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This is a scheme which provides up to 70% support for sustainability projects, which is higher than for other project categories.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Beyond opening up a new revenue stream, the platform has facilitated the use of pre-owned steel instead of new steel and helping this company, whom I have met before, save about 25,000 tonnes of carbon emissions in its first year.

sections.label: MAS green financing schemes
sections.summary: Local companies can use MAS' Sustainable Loan Grant and Bond Grant Schemes for green and transition financing and to defray external review costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: And local companies can use MAS’ Sustainable Loan Grant and Bond Grant Schemes to obtain green and transition financing and to defray the cost of external reviews to validate the sustainability credentials of such loans and bonds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We have also recently expanded our Enterprise Financing Scheme – Green, which provides enhanced risk share to catalyse lending to SMEs, with around $350 million in green loans to date.

sections.label: Carbon Markets Academy of Singapore
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore and EDB partnered NTU to establish the Carbon Markets Academy of Singapore, training 300 professionals over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore and EDB also recently partnered the Nanyang Technological University to establish the Carbon Markets Academy of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This will offer courses to train 300 professionals to take on jobs in the carbon services and trading sector over the next three years.

sections.label: Green transition as must do
sections.summary: Advancing the green transition is a must do to secure the survival of Singapore as an island nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Advancing the green transition is not just a good to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: It is a must do, if we are to secure the survival of our island nation.
